title: Support of a finite type quasi-coherent module and of its pullback
statement:
Let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module of finite type [pqf-def-coherent] on a scheme $X$ [def-pc-scheme], with stalks $\mathcal F_x$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], residue fields $\kappa(x)$ [def-weil-residue-field] and support $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)=\{x:\mathcal F_x
eq0\}$ [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base]. (1) $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$ is closed in $X$. (2) For $x\in X$: $x\in\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)\iff\mathcal F_x
e0\iff\mathcal F_x\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}\kappa(x)
e0$. (3) For every morphism of schemes $f:Y	o X$ the pullback $f^*\mathcal F$ [def-pc-module-pullback] is of finite type and $\operatorname{Supp}(f^*\mathcal F)=f^{-1}(\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal F)$.

proof.text: For any sheaf of rings on the open-set site of an arbitrary topological space, finite type restricts to every open (the proved helper finiteType_over_ringSheaf, generalizing the scheme-only private helper). Specialize this to the scheme structure sheaf: pull the local generating cover back along the slice-site forgetful functor; the induced local pushforward preserves colimits and the unit, hence preserves the finite generating epimorphisms. Choose an affine neighbourhood U of x [def-pc-scheme]. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine], F(U) is finite. Take a finite spanning family and its germs. Span induction using compatibility of germs with addition and scalar multiplication shows that every section germ lies in their stalk-ring span. The additive localization isomorphism and denominator formula of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-module-support-closed] express each stalk element as e(m/s). The image of s in the stalk ring is a unit (the affine stalk ring is the localization at the corresponding prime). Since s times e(m/s) is the germ of m, the span contains e(m/s). Thus the germs generate the stalk finitely.

Apply the zero-module tensor form of Nakayama [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators], Mathlib IsLocalRing.subsingleton_tensorProduct, to the finite stalk and its residue field [def-weil-residue-field]. Taking negations gives the second conjunct.

The pullback is finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-finite-type]. For its stalk at y use [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-pullback]. Finite generation is preserved by scalar extension (Mathlib Module.Finite.base_change) and by a linear isomorphism, so this stalk is finite without using quasi-coherence of the pullback.

Let a be the local stalk map and b the residue map upstairs, and c the residue map downstairs and d the induced residue-field map. Locality [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism] gives b composed with a = d composed with c (Mathlib Scheme.residue_residueFieldMap). Extend the stalk isomorphism to the upstairs residue field, and apply ModuleCat.extendScalarsComp to both compositions. This identifies the pullback residue fibre with extension of the original residue fibre along d. Scalar extension of vector spaces to a field is faithfully flat, hence reflects and preserves the zero module (Mathlib Module.FaithfullyFlat.subsingleton_tensorProduct_iff_right).
Apply Nakayama to both finite stalks. Compose the resulting nonzero-stalk/residue-fibre equivalences with the fibre comparison. Set extensionality gives precisely the inverse-image equality.

lean.statement: theorem finiteType_module_support_pullback {X : Scheme.{u}} (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType] : IsClosed {x : X | ¬ Subsingleton (F.presheaf.stalk x)} ∧ (∀ x : X, ¬ Subsingleton (F.presheaf.stalk x) ↔ ¬ Subsingleton (residueFiber F x)) ∧ ∀ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (f : Y ⟶ X), ((tensorPullback f).obj F).IsFiniteType ∧ {y : Y | ¬ Subsingleton (((tensorPullback f).obj F).presheaf.stalk y)} = f.base ⁻¹' {x : X | ¬ Subsingleton (F.presheaf.stalk x)}
